adaptation.method: per-action contact-aware retargeting; no global pose scale
requiredChanges: Old free-foot ankle targets were generated by leg(88,92); regenerate with new thigh/shin lengths and preserve those angles as the starting intent.
Head/cushion and lower shoulder/floor contacts are world relationships; adjust body placement and cushion from actual new mesh.
Top arm shoulder pivots are unchanged, but waist/chest transformation differs; inspect the entire arm sweep.
adaptation.handAcceptance: This action has not been visually inspected with the selected body/hand setup.
adaptation.implemented: Recomputed both 90-degree bent free legs from current segment lengths; pelvis/world and waist references preserve upper-body position.
adaptation.rotationPolicy: Full forearm axial sharing avoids half-angle +/-pi branch flips; actual-render rotation and visible deformation checks remain required.
adaptation.visualCorrection: Shorten unreachable wrist targets to current arm lengths; retain historical source and QA.

reviewPlan.primaryView: Lower the near-overhead source direction to show opening arm and fixed knee stack together.
checks: Knees remain stacked during thoracic opening.
Head cushion supports the head without intersection.
Elevated side view shows the top arm arc, chest rotation and stationary lower body.
Inspect actual wrist and ankle quaternion paths at every frame, not only endpoint directions: shortest consecutive rotation, total turn, hand/sole facing, left/right consistency and loop seam.
reviewPlan.contentBounds: union of visible body and necessary props over all output frames; one rectangle for the whole clip
reviewPlan.groundProps: Keep necessary support mat/wall/cushion as explicit props; exclude shadow/stage helpers.

limits: This checks authored descriptor vectors and raw foot angles. It does not measure actual wrist/ankle bone quaternions, IK pole branch changes or skinned twists.
Large raw Euler angles or identical endpoint orientations alone do not establish a defect. Root GPU capture must inspect actual continuous rotations.

risks: Head cushion, stacked-leg contact and top-arm sweep need GPU surface inspection.
Other thoracic-rotation positions cover related mechanisms; retain this side-lying variant without calling it a newly invented mechanism.
Current body retains v3 legs/trunk; changing the runtime label alone does not retarget old absolute coordinates.
Support, relaxed, assist and non-dumbbell native grips require their own rendered checks; fixed dumbbell acceptance does not apply.

appearance.purpose: Visual cue for target muscle effort, not a physiological measurement
